items.title: Turning TS2Vec into a Foundation Model for Time Series Classification
items.summary: TS2Vec is one of the strongest self-supervised methods for time series classification, introduced in 2022. It is designed to be trained anew on every dataset: self-supervised pre-training followed by linear probing. Since then, the field has shifted towards foundation models that reuse one encoder across datasets. Yet TS2Vec offers a compact convolutional architecture that operates directly on temporal samples and accepts variable-length inputs without resampling. We ask whether these properties can be retained when the encoder is pre-trained only once, and show that they can: TS2Vec can essentially be turned into a foundation model. Three changes suffice: pre-train on a synthetic corpus,…

items.title: Monopole stability of time-dependent, spherically symmetric backgrounds in Horndeski theory
items.summary: We study linear perturbations about an arbitrary time-dependent, spherically symmetric background in the most general Horndeski theory. The odd-parity sector of such perturbations, analyzed previously, contains no scalar field perturbation and, hence, leaves the related degree of freedom unconstrained. In this paper, we address this issue by analyzing even-parity monopole ($\ell = 0$) perturbations, which isolate this degree of freedom. We derive the quadratic master action for the only propagating physical mode associated with the scalar field and formulate stability criteria which ensure the absence of ghost and radial gradient instabilities for the high-energy modes. These conditions…

items.title: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding
items.summary: Collaborative perception enables agents to retrieve the scene semantics and geometry beyond the field of view of any individual agent. This broader scene understanding enhances transportation safety and improves efficiency in multi-robot systems. However, existing collaborative semantic occupancy methods rely on dense 3D voxel annotations and are limited to recognizing objects within a predefined set of semantic classes. To overcome these limitations, we present CoGaussian, an open-vocabulary Gaussian-based collaborative semantic occupancy prediction framework. CoGaussian represents a scene as a set of foundation model-aligned sparse 3D Gaussians, which serve as a compact representation…

items.title: Cosmological correlators from the Euclidean sphere
items.summary: We propose a new framework for computing late-time cosmological correlators in de Sitter spacetime by analytic continuation from the Euclidean sphere. In this framework, correlators of arbitrary massive scalar fields take the universal form of generalized Euler integrals. Using this representation, we reproduce the results obtained using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism for a range of tree-level and loop diagrams, providing nontrivial checks of the equivalence between the Euclidean and the in-in formalisms. We further show that a Landau analysis of the generalized Euler integrals determines the singularities of the corresponding correlators in momentum space. This framework provides a…

items.title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: Deep State-Space Models (Deep SSMs) have shown promising performance and computational benefits in processing of time-series data with complex temporal dependencies. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute a biologically inspired class of deep SSMs, where computing blocks communicate through spikes, discrete single-bit events rather than continuous activation functions. A particularly important task in time-series processing is forecasting, i.e. predicting future values of a sequence from past observations alone. However, how to best perform forecasting with SNNs is an open question, where the standard autoregressive nature of the data processing with SNNs requires values that are not…

items.title: The "Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery" Workshop: A Community Roadmap for the Future of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory After the LSST
items.summary: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will complete its ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in the mid-2030s. Its 8.4 m aperture and 9.6 square degree field of view give it an étendue unmatched by any facility planned for that era. The Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery workshop (KIPAC/SLAC, 3-5 August 2026) brought together approximately 100 participants to discuss Rubin's future after LSST. This paper summarizes the workshop's structure and discussions across five working groups. The continued-surveying group explored a machine-learning foundation model pretrained on Rubin imaging for detection, deblending, and classification. The cadence group considered allocating…

items.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
items.summary: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for…

items.summary: In this work, we investigate the correspondence between quasinormal modes (QNMs) and greybody factors (GBFs) in higher-dimensional Reissner--Nordstöm--de Sitter black holes based on the massless scalar field. Our analysis focuses on the QNMs in the near-ultracold family where the inner, outer, and cosmological horizons are close together. Under the geometric limit condition, the leading-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin term of the QNM is dominant for fixed angular quantum numbers and dimensionality without imposing the eikonal limit. items.title: Towards Consistent Geospatial Representations: Aligning One Encoder to Many Foundation Models
items.summary: Geospatial foundation models (GFMs) differ widely in pretraining objective, modality and resolution, and none leads across benchmarks. We ask whether their representations are complementary, and whether a single encoder can inherit that complementarity. We introduce Pangaea-Latents, an extension of the Pangaea benchmark providing frozen embeddings of $5$ GFMs over its $11$ datasets, along with reproduced baselines, and find GFM embeddings to be neither redundant nor disjoint. We then propose GeoMixture, a preliminary framework to align a ViT to several GFMs per dataset through a multi-representation alignment (mREPA) objective. items.title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.summary: Monitoring the chain-of-thought (CoT) of language models (LMs) is a key strategy for detecting and preventing misbehaviors for AI safety. As such, it is critical to identify reinforcement learning (RL) practices that lead to unmonitorable chain-of-thought. One such practice may be unavoidable: reward misspecification. As RL environments become more complex, it is infeasible to have perfect verification, and models are rewarded for behaviors that are different from the true task intent. We show that reward misspecification alone already degrades monitorability. items.title: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI
items.summary: Adapting Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) to medical imaging via LoRA has become standard practice, yet model selection is guided almost entirely by downstream task metrics, treating backbones with similar performance as interchangeable. We investigate whether equal performance implies equal internal representational shift. We analyse four ViT-B/16 backbones, DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM, and BiomedCLIP, pre-trained with different objectives (self-distillation vs. contrastive vision-language) and on different data domains (natural vs. medical images). We adapt each to brain tumour segmentation and evaluate on six datasets covering both segmentation and Alzheimer's disease classification.…

items.title: MaD-RSI: Model-as-Data for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) of agent harnesses has emerged as an effective approach to enhancing the capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents. By searching the harness space for a specific LLM on a given dataset, RSI can discover a harness tailored to the capabilities and behavioral characteristics of that model. However, such optimization often creates a strong coupling between the learned harness and its target LLM, limiting generalization across models and requiring substantial computational resources to adapt to new LLMs. Moreover, existing RSI methods typically optimize a harness using feedback from a single model and evaluate its generalization to other models only…

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
items.summary: Accurate electrical load forecasting supports power-system operation across countries, regions, cities, and buildings, but repeated development of target-specific models is costly. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) provide reusable pretrained backbones, although multi-domain pretraining may not fully capture load-specific characteristics. This paper compares pretrained inference, full fine-tuning, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) in terms of forecasting accuracy and adaptation efficiency across four electrical load aggregation levels. MOIRAI 1.0 Large serves as the primary backbone, while Chronos-2 assesses whether the findings transfer across model families. The evaluation covers both…

items.title: From Predictive Geometry to Action: Learning Complementary Predictive Representations for Embodied Manipulation
items.summary: Effective manipulation requires a policy to capture not only about the current scene geometry, but also about how that geometry will evolve under interaction. Existing approaches either augment policies with geometric information from current observations or introduce future prediction as auxiliary supervision, leaving open how predictive geometry should be represented for action generation. Therefore, we propose a two-stage framework, which learns complementary predictive representations from multi-view video clips. items.title: Robust Representation Learning for Spiking Neural Networks based on Conditional Information Bottleneck
items.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have shown great potential for low-power neuromorphic computing due to their event-driven processing and spatiotemporal sparsity, but they remain vulnerable to input perturbations, hardware-intrinsic noise, and adversarial attacks in real-world deployment. We attribute this vulnerability partly to input-specific hidden representations learned by standard SNNs trained with conventional cross-entropy loss, as our information-plane analysis empirically shows that substantial input-related information can still be retained after label-predictive information becomes stable. items.title: IECG: Weakly-Supervised Interpretability-Enhancing Foundation Model for Electrocardiogram
items.summary: Electrocardiography (ECG) is a cornerstone of cardiac diagnosis, yet most machine learning methods for ECG analysis lack interpretability, limiting their clinical adoption. We present IECG, a weakly-supervised ECG foundation model that jointly performs diagnostic classification and abnormality localization without requiring manual abnormal region annotations, overcoming a long-standing bottleneck in interpretable ECG learning. Central to IECG is a weakly-supervised attention strategy that explicitly incorporates clinical priors by deriving abnormality heatmap pseudo-labels from established ECG clinical knowledge. items.title: Relativistic Strong Quantum Mpemba Effect
items.summary: The Unruh effect links acceleration to thermalization, providing a relativistic setting for anomalous quantum relaxation. We demonstrate a {\it relativistic} strong quantum Mpemba effect in the Unruh thermalization of a two-level detector coupled to a massless scalar field. For a fixed pair of isospectral initial states, relaxation curves that never cross in inertial motion exhibit a Mpemba crossing above a threshold acceleration. items.title: AdaptMIL: Domain Adaptation for Multiple Instance Learning in Digital Pathology
items.summary: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) support a wide range of histopathology tasks on whole-slide images through multiple instance learning (MIL). Despite recent progress, these models remain sensitive to cross-hospital distribution shifts: performance often degrades when a task head (e.g., classification) is trained on data from one hospital and then used on data from another hospital. To address this challenge, we propose AdaptMIL, a training strategy for integrating domain adaptation into MIL training. items.title: Staged Continual Adaptation of Multimodal Foundation Models for Japanese Financial Documents
items.summary: Staged post-training of multimodal foundation models chains vision-language alignment, reasoning distillation, and domain tuning, yet how each phase trades capabilities against the others remains under-characterised. items.title: Elicitation or Expansion? Demystifying Gains from Agent Harness Optimization
items.summary: Recent studies in harness optimization have shown substantial performance gains in language model agents without updating model weights. A well-designed harness more effectively leverages the underlying model's capabilities by shaping context, tool use, and execution workflows. However, naïve success rates alone do not fully characterize whether optimized harness yields more reliable success on tasks already within reach (elicitation) or a broader range of solvable tasks (expansion). This distinction is crucial for recursive self-improvement and evolutionary search, as expansion may provide a broader range of successful experiences to push the capability boundaries. items.title: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality. However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should. A misaligned model training its successor can shape what that successor knows, how it behaves, and what it wants, and the harm carries forward into the next generation. We study this risk through the lens of AI control. items.title: Ensemble-Aware Structural Encoding (EASE): Conditioning Protein Encoders on Peptide Conformational Ensembles
items.summary: Protein foundation models provide transferable representations for downstream peptide prediction tasks. However, existing representations typically reduce a peptide to a single sequence or structure, which may miss conformational variability relevant to key peptide properties, including antibacterial activity, hemolysis, toxicity, stability, and binding. For example, protease resistance correlates more strongly with conformational dynamics measured by hydrogen exchange than with average helicity. items.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) promises AI systems, such as self-evolving LLM agents, that become better at producing further improvements. Evaluating this promise requires separating product claims about the final system from process claims about the improvement process itself. Existing surveys specify the evidence these claims require, but how often studies report that evidence remains unmeasured. We examine this question through full-text coding of 114 eligible studies in a reproducible arXiv search frame frozen in October 2026, including 90 that describe their own systems as RSI. items.title: Responsible AI In Credit Portfolio Growth: A Risk-Controlled Framework For Artificial Intelligence–Driven Lending In U.S. Banks
items.summary: This study develops and validates GUARD (Governance, Underwriting integrity, Accountability, Resilience, Disclosure), a risk-controlled framework for the deployment of artificial intelligence in credit origination and portfolio management by U.S. banking organizations. It examines how lenders can convert AI-driven underwriting into sustained credit portfolio growth while retaining defensible control over fair lending exposure, model risk, and consumer explanation obligations, in a supervisory environment that between April 2025 and June 2026 moved decisively from prescriptive to principles-based expectations.

items.title: Bi-Level Harness Optimization and Textual Backpropagation in Autonomous 4-Loop Recursive Self-Improvement Engines
The rise of super-emotional intelligence

But also in honeybees, this progress requires tools capable of resolving weak, magnetically induced neural activity with high spatio-temporal precision. The approach, presented here, bridges quantum biology and neuroscience, aiming at testing the…

items.title: Toward quantum-informed addiction medicine: Coherence, entangled-photon imaging, and a theranostic hypothesis.
items.summary: Background Quantum biology has shown that selected biological processes depend on quantum effects, including coherence, tunnelling, and spin-dependent reactions. In parallel, quantum imaging now uses entangled photons to extract biological information at low photon flux. Early evidence that biological tissue can alter photon entanglement in disease-associated ways raises a translational question: whether decoherence itself can become a diagnostic signal. Rationale Addiction is a disorder of reward-circuit function in which current imaging can define anatomy and network activity but cannot resolve molecular-scale information processing in affected tissue. items.title: Deterministic Finite-Scale Geometry of RNA Language Model Embeddings Predicts siRNA Efficacy: G ϵ (r) Outperforms LID as a Functional Complexity Measure
items.summary: Motivation. BLAST-based screening of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) frequently produces false positives in the “grey zone”, where alignment statistics are marginally significant but functional affinity is low. Existing approaches based on local intrinsic dimensionality (LID) of language model embeddings are unstable on small datasets and high-dimensional representations. Results. We introduce a deterministic finite-scale geometric index Gϵ(r), constructed from the volume of hyperbolic balls in the Poincaré ball Bn, and apply it to messenger RNA (mRNA) target embeddings obtained from the RNA foundation model RNA-FM. items.title: Neural state reduction: a quantum-inspired framework for how latent conscious thought becomes reportable.
items.summary: Human conscious thought often appears as a diffuse, unstable, and only partly verbalizable field until attention, questioning, decision, or speech stabilizes it into a reportable form. This manuscript develops a quantum-inspired neural framework for that transition. The proposal does not claim that consciousness literally depends on microscopic quantum computation, that the brain implements a physical quantum computer, or that neuronal tissue maintains macroscopic quantum coherence. items.title: Quantum coherent dynamics in allophycocyanin trimer complex.
items.summary: For years, scientists have debated whether plants and algae use quantum coherence to enhance the transfer of light energy during photosynthesis. Some studies have suggested that wavelike quantum effects might help energy flow more efficiently between pigments. To investigate this idea, we studied allophycocyanin (APC), a light-harvesting protein complex found in cyanobacteria. Using a combination of ultrafast laser spectroscopic methods and rigorous hierarchical equations-of-motion simulations, we examined both the trimer protein complex and its monomer subunit.
